executive_summary.narrative:
82 hypotheses tested, 16 proven and reported. Unproven candidates are in the raw artifacts, not shown as findings.

Juice Shop exhibits several critical vulnerabilities that directly compromise its core authentication and authorization systems. The most severe issues include SQL injection in login and search endpoints, along with unauthenticated access to administrative configuration data. These proven attack vectors provide full control over user accounts and expose sensitive application data, representing immediate risks that require urgent remediation. High-severity vulnerabilities like reflected XSS and security question enumeration further weaken the platform's defenses. All findings represent confirmed exploits rather than theoretical weaknesses, warranting high confidence in these critical risk assessments.

findings.title: SQL Injection in User Login
findings.status: confirmed exploitable (4 proof(s); merged from 4 hypotheses)
findings.recommendation: Successful exploitation allows full account takeover and unauthorized access to all user accounts. Implement parameterized queries or prepared statements for all database operations. Sanitize and validate all user inputs, especially in authentication endpoints. Apply principle of least privilege for database connections used by the application.

findings.title: Admin Configuration Access Without Authentication
findings.status: confirmed exploitable (2 proof(s); merged from 2 hypotheses)
findings.recommendation: Unauthenticated attackers can access sensitive application configuration details that may reveal infrastructure information and secrets. Implement proper role-based access controls (RBAC) for administrative endpoints. Add authentication checks and validate user permissions before serving configuration data. Restrict access to administrative endpoints using IP whitelisting where appropriate.

Validate and sanitize search input parameters.

Implement rate limiting and account lockout mechanisms for security question requests. Require authentication to access security question endpoints. Return generic responses for invalid email addresses and randomize security question IDs to prevent enumeration.
